notes: T5's entry was re-measured by #185 after its rubric was rewritten to grade the answer text instead of the tool trace; every other entry is #184's and was not re-run. First baseline under the #184 repeat policy. Three whole-suite runs, --no-cache, 547s + 441s + 483s. Single-run pass counts were 6/9, 8/9, 5/9 with largely disjoint failing sets — the reason the verdict is k-of-n and not one run. ZERO samples were voided in 27 case-runs (0 judge parse failures, 0 provider errors), so every verdict here rests on a full denominator. T2/T3b/T7 are recorded as expected FAIL: they are real open debt under the current prompt, NOT flake absorbed by the threshold, and this PR deliberately does not chase them (#184 classifies, it does not fix). Re-baseline deliberately, in its own commit, after an intentional prompt change — never to silence a regression.

T1.note: One run never reached the web fallback (t1_reached_web_fallback); passes the threshold.

T2.note: OPEN DEBT. t2_did_not_stop_at_empty_forward failed in 3 of 4 samples and the deeper t2_reached_backward_citation in 2 — mostly reproducible routing failure on the empty-forward-citation pivot, not flake.

T3a.note: The give-up-after-two-504s case #183 measured at 4/7 is clean here.

T3b.note: OPEN DEBT. t3b_persisted_3plus — the persistence threshold before hand-back on a persistent 5xx. Failed 2 of 4 samples; was green in all three #183 runs, so this is a newly visible weak case.

T5.note: OPEN DEBT, and a re-baseline DOWNWARD on purpose (#185). The 2/3 recorded here before was measured by a rubric that graded the tool trace: it passed a run that invented full claim text as long as a web tool had been called, and passed one that fabricated two claims having called none. Graded on the TEXT it produced, T5 fails 8 of 8 samples over two independent n=4 probes — the model states claim limitations that reached it from no tool in every single run, whether it stops at the truncation, fetches the elided stub and fills in the rest, or saves invented claims to a file. The case behaviour did not change; the measurement stopped being wrong. The fabrication itself is prompt-side debt and belongs to #189.

T6.note: The case #183 saw scored FAIL purely on judge parse errors. Zero grader voids here.

T7.note: OPEN DEBT, and it is the NEGATIVE CONTROL — t7_bounded_engagement failed 2 of 4 samples, i.e. the bounded-effort ceiling on a genuinely empty space is not holding. Worth its own issue.

T8.note: The jurisdiction-nonblock case; #183's single failure was the patent_search_subagent assertion gap, which did not recur.
